name: Pierce County Heritage Museum and Depot
unique: A 1903 railroad depot on the National Register holding the county's collection of turpentine, timber and farm tools, in a town that existed because the railroad came through the pine woods.
buzz: Small, free and run by people who know the county. The depot itself is the best building in Blackshear.

name: Blackshear Geo Tour
customer: Geology people, science teachers, road trippers
unique: A self guided tour of the county's geological oddities, including the shoreline features of an ancient sea and the sand and clay deposits that made this flat pine country, mapped and signed by the county.
buzz: A genuinely unusual thing for a rural county to publish. Almost nobody drives it, which means you have the stops to yourself.

name: Pecan Festival of Georgia
unique: A one day harvest festival in downtown Blackshear with pecan pies, vendors, a parade and a pageant, celebrating the crop that still pays in this part of south Georgia.
buzz: The pie contest and the boiled peanuts are the local draw. Free, crowded and over by dark.

name: Shiloh Primitive Baptist Church
unique: A white frame country church in the Pierce County woods with a cemetery of the families who cleared this land, kept up by a congregation that still meets a few times a year.
buzz: Quiet, unaltered and easy to miss from the road. Photographers come for the light through the windows.

name: Lanahassee Creek Wildlife Management Area
unique: More than four thousand acres of state owned pine and hardwood creek bottom in one of the least populated counties in Georgia, with deer, turkey and quail hunting and no facilities at all.
buzz: Locals hunt it and almost nobody else knows it exists. Bring water, boots and a compass, because there is no trail system.

name: Preston Peanut Festival
unique: The county's one big day, with peanuts boiled and candied, a parade and the kind of crowd where everybody knows the person behind the booth.
buzz: Tiny and entirely local. If you are counting Georgia festivals this is the one almost nobody has been to.

name: Webster County Courthouse
unique: A courthouse on the square in Preston, the county's only town, in a county of fewer than two thousand people that was carved out of Sumter and Stewart in 1853.
buzz: Ten minutes and you have seen downtown. The point is that it is still here at all.

name: Cusseta Courthouse Square
unique: A tiny consolidated city-county square beside the Army post that swallowed most of the county's land, with the historical marker explaining how a farming county became a military reservation.
buzz: The square is a block and the story is the whole county. Pair it with the river and you have seen Cusseta.

name: Uchee Creek Campground and Marina
customer: Military families, veterans, anglers with access
unique: A campground, cabins and marina on the Chattahoochee inside the Army reservation, with river frontage, a boat ramp and the kind of quiet that comes from a gate check at the entrance.
buzz: Reviews from military families rate it as one of the better MWR campgrounds in the southeast. Civilians cannot use it, so check eligibility before planning around it.

name: Bell Witch Cave
dates: Weekends May to December, October nightly
customer: Ghost story people, families, October crowds
unique: A cave and the reconstructed John Bell cabin on the farm where the Bell family reported a haunting from 1817 to 1821, the story that became the best known ghost tale in the South, run by the family that owns the land.
buzz: Guides tell the documented history first and the reports second, which makes it better than a haunted house. October sells out and the lantern tours book by appointment.

name: Bell Witch Fall Festival
unique: Five weeks of staged productions in Adams including an outdoor drama about the Bell Witch, put on by a community theater group in the town where the story happened.
buzz: The outdoor show is the one people come back for. Small cast, real fields, and a story the audience already knows.

name: Tennessee-Kentucky Threshing Show
customer: Tractor people, families, farm history buffs
unique: Steam engines, thrashing machines and horse drawn equipment run for a crowd on Highway 41, with sawmilling and plowing demonstrations rather than a static show.
buzz: The steam whistle and the working equipment draw people from both states. It is loud, hot and exactly what a farm show should be.

name: Robertson County Fair
unique: A county fair on the Springfield fairgrounds with livestock shows, a demolition derby, tractor pulls and a midway, in the middle of Tennessee's dark fired tobacco country.
buzz: The demo derby and the livestock barns are the local priorities. Cheap, hot and busy every night.

name: Historic Springfield Square
unique: A courthouse square of 1890s commercial buildings in a tobacco market town, with the old depot and a block of shops that have not been rebuilt into anything else.
buzz: Quiet most days. The square is the place to eat if you are passing through on Highway 41.

name: Historic Rock Castle
unique: A limestone plantation house begun in the 1780s by Daniel Smith, surveyor of the Tennessee frontier, standing on the Cumberland River with its original outbuildings and a family cemetery.
buzz: One of the oldest houses in middle Tennessee and rarely crowded. The river setting and the stone walls are what people remember.

name: Monthaven Arts and Cultural Center
unique: An antebellum mansion with Civil War graffiti on its walls, now an arts center with rotating exhibitions, studios and a garden, so you get the house and the art in one stop.
buzz: The penciled names of Union soldiers on the upstairs walls stop people cold. Programming is stronger than a suburban arts center usually manages.

name: Bledsoe Creek State Park
unique: A small park on a creek arm of Old Hickory Lake with a campground, boat ramp, fishing piers and a hardwood ridge trail, twenty five minutes from Nashville and never as busy as it should be.
buzz: Campers rate the sites and the water access. Herons, osprey and the occasional eagle are routine.

name: Hendersonville Memory Gardens
unique: The cemetery where Johnny Cash and June Carter Cash are buried, in the town they lived in for thirty five years, with fans leaving guitar picks and coins on the stone.
buzz: People come from other countries. It is a working cemetery, so keep it quiet and do not treat it as a photo set.

name: Sumner County Museum
unique: A county museum with a reconstructed log cabin, a country store, war collections and the papers of the families who settled the Cumberland bend, kept by the historical society.
buzz: Old fashioned in the best sense and cheap. The volunteers will talk your ear off about Gallatin's role in the Civil War.

name: Old Hickory Lake
dates: Year round, best May to October
unique: Twenty two thousand acres of the Cumberland impounded behind Old Hickory Dam, with marinas, Corps parks and a bass and crappie fishery right against Nashville's northern suburbs.
buzz: The lake is how half of Sumner County spends summer. Weekday evenings on the water are the local reward for living here.

name: Fiddlers Grove Historic Village
cost: Free with fair admission, otherwise free
dates: Open during the fair and by appointment
company: Wilson County / James E. Ward Agricultural Center
unique: A village of two dozen restored nineteenth century Wilson County buildings, log cabins, a school, a church and a cotton gin, reassembled on the fairgrounds and staffed by volunteers in period dress.
buzz: The living history days and the fair are when it is fully open. Kids get to handle the tools, which is the whole idea.

name: Wilson County Fair and Tennessee State Fair
company: Wilson County Fair / Tennessee State Fair
unique: Ten days that now serve as both the Wilson County Fair and the Tennessee State Fair, drawing close to eight hundred thousand people to livestock shows, a draft horse pull, motorsport and free concerts.
buzz: Locals call it the biggest ten days in the state and the crowds back it up. The agricultural exhibits are still the core, not a sideshow.

name: Cedars of Lebanon State Park
unique: A park on a cedar glade, a rare limestone barren with shallow soil and plants found almost nowhere else, with caves, sinkholes, miles of trail and a campground inside an hour of Nashville.
buzz: The glades are the botanical draw and the trails are easy enough for kids. Spring wildflowers bring the naturalists out.

name: Nashville Superspeedway
unique: A 1.33 mile concrete oval outside Lebanon that brought NASCAR Cup racing back to middle Tennessee, with infield access and a track that hosts driving experiences on non race days.
buzz: Concrete makes for hard racing and the June weekend has become a fixture. The infield is where the parties are.

name: Silver Ridge Pottery
customer: Craft people, gift shoppers, couples on a date
unique: A working pottery studio outside Lebanon where the potter throws and fires on site, sells food safe ware and teaches wheel classes to people who have never touched clay.
buzz: The classes are the reason to book ahead. Visitors say the potter explains the firing without talking down to anyone.

name: Watertown Depot and Square
customer: Railfans, small town walkers, antique hunters
unique: A railroad town with a depot, a wide main street and a cluster of antique shops, sitting between Lebanon and Smithville in the rolling country east of Nashville.
buzz: The antique shops and the depot are the whole stop. It is quiet, and the town likes it that way.
